title: SRE weekly update 2026-08-01
body:
Summary:
- Period: 2026-07-25 -> 2026-07-31
- Owner: Aisha Patel (SRE manager)
- Focus this week: incident triage and mitigation, SLO review for hosted-api, on-call process improvements, cleanup of stale runbooks.

Incidents and major events:
1) P1: Hosted API partial degradation (2026-07-29 03:14 - 2026-07-29 05:02 UTC)
   - Symptom: Increased 5xx rates and spikes in request latency for hosted-api region us-west-2. Customer-facing errors ~3.8% at peak.
   - Impact: Short-lived partial disruption for ~15% of requests routed to a subset of serving nodes; majority of traffic served normally via fallback routing.
   - Root cause (preliminary): Regression in the autoscaler introduced in PR #987 - a corner case caused the scale-down decision to be overly aggressive under a specific cache-warmup pattern. When nodes were scaled down, some in-memory cache priming failed and subsequent requests hit cold paths increasing latency and error rates.
   - Mitigation: Rollback of autoscaler change at 04:05 UTC restored normal behavior; manual warmup job run to repopulate KV caches; traffic gradually returned to normal.
   - Follow-ups (owner assignments):
     * Infra: Add a canary flag for autoscaler changes + tighter rollout (Miguel Torres). Due: 2026-08-07.
     * Serving runtime: Add explicit warmup probe and ensure scale-down waits for KV-cache eviction window (Priya Raman). Due: 2026-08-14.
     * SLO/product: Draft customer communication + post-incident summary (Aisha Patel). Due: 2026-08-05.
   - Notes: No customer data exposure. Observability gaps: missing a simple pre-scale-down warmup metric; will add a health-check that simulates short prefix generation to catch cold-cache regressions.

2) P2: Dedicated cluster scheduling lag (2026-07-27 11:40 - 2026-07-27 13:10 UTC)
   - Symptom: Jobs queued for longer than expected during a regional maintenance window leading to slower batch job starts.
   - Mitigation and RCA: A mismatched version of the scheduler had a degraded backoff algorithm (failed to re-enqueue jobs promptly). Patch deployed same day.
   - Follow-ups: Add integration test to simulate maintenance window + job queuing behavior (Connor Lee). Due: 2026-08-10.

SLOs and Error Budget status:
- Hosted API latency SLOs (p50/p90/p99): currently meeting p50/p90; p99 breached on 2026-07-29 during the incident.
- Error budget consumption this 28d window: 2.4% (target <5%). The P1 used ~0.6% of the budget.
- Availability: 99.96% for the last 30 days (target 99.95%). Still within SLA but monitor p99 tail volatility.
- Action: Run SLO burn-down review on 2026-08-04 to decide on temporary throttling or additional reserve capacity for anticipated traffic next quarter. (Owner: Aisha Patel)

On-call handoffs / runbook notes:
- This week's on-call rotation:
  * Week start (2026-07-25): On-call primary: Samir Gupta; secondary: Lina Wu.
  * Week end (2026-07-31): Handoff to next rotation: Primary: Jordan Kim; secondary: Priya Raman.
- Observations from handoffs: Please keep runbook step "force-warmup-kv" in top-level checklist; some new responders missed this leading to longer mitigation time. Action: Add a short checklist card in PagerDuty templates (Miguel Torres). Due: 2026-08-05.
- On-call tooling update: We rolled out the new incident CLI helper to a small group; feedback: helpful but needs clearer errors when failing to post anchors to the incident doc (UX follow-up: add retry + clearer logging).

Operational/maintenance work completed:
- Cleaned up ~20 stale service accounts used solely for CI access (security+cost).
- Upgraded monitoring agent on dedicated pools in eu-west-1 (no regressions observed).
- Small infra cost-saving: adjusted default VM sizes for non-critical batch workers (expected monthly savings ~$4.5k).

Upcoming work / blockers:
- Autoscaler canary + rollout improvements (blocked by final sign-off on new rollback playbook).
- SLO review meeting scheduled 2026-08-04 (invite sent to eng product and support).
- Private deployment audits: awaiting customer-provided test artifacts before running smoke tests (expected by 2026-08-09).

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Miguel Torres: Implement autoscaler canary flag + PagerDuty template checklist. Due 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-05 respectively.
- Priya Raman: Add warmup probe and scale-down guard in serving runtime; update runbook. Due 2026-08-14.
- Connor Lee: Add queued-job integration test for scheduler. Due 2026-08-10.
- Aisha Patel: Draft customer-facing incident summary + run SLO burn-down meeting. Due 2026-08-05 and 2026-08-04.

Meeting notes / syncs this week:
- 2026-07-28: Post-incident sync with infra, serving-runtime, and product. Key decisions: pause non-critical infra rollouts for 72h post-rollback; create a joint taskforce to look at cold-start patterns.
- 2026-07-30: On-call retrospective: identified gaps in runbook discoverability and incident doc anchoring. Small wins: quicker escalation to secondary when primary busy; CLI helper reduced doc creation time by ~40%.

Runbooks / docs touched this week:
- Updated: runbooks/force-warmup-kv.md (added quick command and smoke-check).
- New draft: autoscaler-canary-playbook.md (needs review).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Follow up with observability team to add a synthetic KV-warmup probe in the canary region.
- Coordinate with product to prioritize top-10 customers for proactive notification if error budget crosses 3%.
- Add a short internal training for on-call responders on warmup steps (30m).

Appendix: short metrics snapshot (last 7d)
- 99th latency (hosted-api, us-west-2): 320ms (median 65ms).
- 5xx rate (hosted-api, peak during incident): 3.8% -> baseline 0.05%.
- Error budget (28d): 2.4% consumed.

If you have questions or want this summarized into a short blurb for the executive weekly, ping me and I'll extract the 3-line summary.

-- Aisha
